BEST_BET.rationale: It is the only concept whose step on a mission axis survived the red team at about 10x. Delivered energy is 0.37 vs 3.95 pJ/bit against HBM, or 11x (5.5x with random placement, 15x at 1 mm). That saves ~92 W/GPU at the 16-tier x 1 b planning case (78 GB/GPU; range 48-169 W). The cell is refresh-light: the 1e-4-tail cell refreshes every ~3.6 s at 105 C, ~225x rarer than Si. CIRC: 'energy win survives any reasonable correction'. The 1 b pass bars are lenient against reported oxide 2T0C retention (>200 s at 95 C): drift <=75 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C. So P(Gate A+ at 1 b) is ~0.5-0.6, the highest P of any concept that still carries a ~10x. AI-accelerator power and the HBM squeeze are the most fundable pain in 2027-28, and ~$1,500 of 5-yr value per GPU covers the ~$650 near-tier cost ~2x. Weaknesses an investor must price: (1) it is not a cost step ($4.6-12/GB); (2) the 2 b capacity (169 W) is unmeasured; (3) TSMC/Intel own the carrier slot and broad claims are barred. So value is captured as qualification data plus narrow IP (bond-interface hydrogen control, cross-temperature MLC, carrier-last contamination package, RTN screen/remap), sold into a foundry or memory-maker JDA or an acquisition, not royalties. My sketch puts P(fundable Series A) at ~0.15, the best in the set (AND-STACK ~0.06). It also fits the team: one oxide-reliability physicist plus one systems founder.
BEST_BET.experiment: Gate A+ (M2-M11). Vertical channel-all-around 2T0C coupons in IGZO, In-poor IGZO, IGO and ZTO, with single vs series write gate and -0.5 vs -0.7 V hold. Each split is measured after the post-bond heat/H sequence AND a real D2O-labelled 350-400 C fusion bond (SIMS H/D, top-tier dVt). On >=1e5 cells/split: drift sigma at 1/10/100 s at 85/105/125 C; write-T1/read-T2 maps (dT +/-30 K) with in-row references; RTN at ~1 s and 1 us-1 ms; the directly measured 1e-4 retention quantile. PASS (1 b planning): drift <=75 mV, RTN 1e-4 quantile <=100 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, bonded dVt <=10 mV. 2 b upside: <=20 mV drift in a >=600 mV window, cross-T residual <=10 mV, RTN <=30 mV, tail <=7.5 aA at 105 C. Then Gate B-lite (M18): tiers on finished logic die, RO shift <=1%, Vt <=10 mV, 1,000 h bake, CSAM and VPD-ICPMS In/Ga/Zn <=1e10 at/cm2.
BEST_BET.cost: ~$240k standalone for Gate A+ (dossier). In this portfolio ~$175k rides on the shared oxide-tail-atlas lot, plus $70k gated for Gate B-lite. The dossier's full standalone plan is $1.00M ($677k experiments).
BEST_BET.kill: M11 (2027-11-30): kill the capacity claim if every split, including the real-bond split, has drift sigma >75 mV at 1 s/105 C (still >75 mV re-measured at 100 ms), OR 1e-4-tail retention <1 s at 105 C (>22.5 aA), OR 1e-4 RTN quantile >100 mV. M18: kill BEOL tiers (carrier-only) if RO shift >1% or Vt >10 mV unrecoverable. Downgrade below 4x if measured bitline+sense energy extrapolates >0.9 pJ/bit at the port. Investor kill: no named BSPDN foundry or accelerator evaluator (Intel 18A/14A, TSMC A16 customer) by M22. Then sell or license the qualification package rather than raise on it.

FASTEST_PROOF.rationale: This is the cheapest, lowest-schedule-risk decisive binary in the portfolio: $124k and 6 months. It needs no fab, no mask and no university nanofab queue, only retired DDR4 and DDR5 RDIMMs on open DRAM Bender and Antmicro testers. It settles two things at once. (a) The commodity claim: ~9x refresh energy on DDR5 RDIMMs at 85 C with chipkill kept (6.1-20x; ~35x at 65 C; ~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL). (b) The raw-BER-1e-4 / 1.88x-margin premise (Cs 5.4 -> 2.7 fF) that MARGIN STACK, PIXEL-STACK, AND-STACK MLC and DIODE-TOWER all budget against. Through the VRT, cluster and dwell-time spectrum, its cluster and VRT statistics become the error model for every cell gate that follows. Investor caveat: on its own this result does not unlock a round. The flag leg is killed, value is ~$3.9 per module over 5 yr, CXL-controller incumbents could replicate it in firmware, and IND calls it 'sound engineering, weak business'. Fund it as portfolio calibration, as a publishable credibility asset (an open DRAM error atlas) and as a hyperscaler door-opener for a retired-DDR4 CXL soak. P(GO) ~0.6.
FASTEST_PROOF.experiment: Phase 1 (M0-M6). 150 retired DDR4 modules are quick-screened (>=30 lots/vendor); 60 are deep-mapped across 1x-1a date codes on 4 DRAM Bender stations at 0.128-4 s x 45/65/85 C x 4 patterns, with RS-8 and BCH-12 scoring. In parallel, >=24 DDR5 1a/1b RDIMMs run on 2 Antmicro testers: JEDEC ECS per-die counts, post-SEC 2-3-bit maps and BEER H-matrix recovery. Also: VRT arrival counts at 1 s/85 C over 1,000 h on 20 modules plus a dwell-time (RTN) spectrum; a failure-mode census (chip/DQ/row/column/MAT); a test of whether a 1 h grade holds for 1,000 h; hammer at relaxed refresh with controller RFM.
FASTEST_PROOF.cost: $124k (dossier Phase 1). $110k in this portfolio, with stations reused. The full 24-month plan is $946k and is not funded here; the CXL soak is a partner or raise milestone.
FASTEST_PROOF.kill: M6 (2027-06-30): kill the commodity relaxed-refresh product if the RS-8 (chipkill) safe interval including VRT over a 1 h scrub is <4x the part's JEDEC window at 65 C (<256 ms DDR4, <128 ms DDR5). Downgrade if multi-chip events are >10%, or if any new mechanism exceeds 2x its 32/64 ms rate. GO requires >=6x the window at 85 C (DDR5 >=0.19 s, DDR4 >=0.38 s), >=24x at 65 C, and the 1 h grade holding for >=95% of modules. If it is killed, every cell concept loses its 1.88x ECC margin and re-plans Cs.

MOONSHOT.rationale: It has the highest ceiling: the only concept whose density and bits/$ step comes from tier count rather than lithography, built with one hole etch on 3D-NAND tool sets. Revised figures: 64 x 2 b gives 2.62 Gb/mm2 = 5.9x 1-beta (8.8x as a two-deck 96 x 2 b part). That is ~2.3x bits/$ vs 2026 1-beta, with ~25x lower refresh power at 1 s and zero EUV. PIXEL-STACK (4.6x, bits/$ ~parity), DIODE-TOWER (3.9x, 1.8x bits/$, P 5-10%) and CHARGE-RIVER (2.5x, cost leg killed) all have lower ceilings after the red team. The risks are real. The single-film closure is topologically impossible (killed). The two-film notched-write-pocket cell needs three unprecedented modules, with P(closure) ~20%. Against a ~2032 incumbent the cost step is only 1.1-1.4x (1.2-1.6x at 96 tiers), so the prize is density. NEO's 3D X-DRAM is ~3 years ahead (1 b PoC Apr 2026, no licensee yet), and the Macronix pillar and SEL NOSRAM estates narrow claims to the notch module, bias scheme, group write and temperature-triggered MLC. But one result would pull a NAND maker (Kioxia/SanDisk, Micron, SK hynix, Macronix) into a JDA and justify a $30-50M round: a 2-tier vertical closure holding 2 b >=1 s at 85 C with CR >=0.57, which NEO has not shown. P(GO#1B) ~0.1-0.15; P(reaching a 64-tier product) ~0.03-0.05.
MOONSHOT.experiment: GO#1A planar statistics (M9), on the shared atlas lot: CR >=0.57 at sigma <=0.045 over >=50 cells; write-FET 1e-4 hold tail <=17 aA at -3.0 V on >=1e4 devices; <=111 fA per unselected cell; 4 levels >=1 s at 85 C with <=78 mV tail drift; cross-T 2 b BER <=1e-4 at dT +/-10 K; <=30 mV after 1e8 own-tier and 1e9 neighbour events; VRT and RTN on >=1e4 cells. Then GO#1B (M14), the decisive gate: a 2-tier vertical closure coupon with 250 nm e-beam holes in SiO2/poly-SiGe/SiO2/SiN, two-film notched write pocket. It must show write-then-read on >=2 tiers with no ring-to-read-channel short, ring hold <=100 aA at 85 C with write plate at -3.0 V, per-tier CR >=0.57, and FIB/TEM of the notch contact. The 32-tier dummy etch coupon and 4-tier stack are raise milestones.
MOONSHOT.cost: ~$0.4M of direct spend to GO#1B standalone (dossier plan $970k/24 months). In this portfolio: $35k planar split on the atlas lot plus $120k for the closure coupon, released only at the M9 gate.
MOONSHOT.kill: Kill at M9 if CR <0.40, write-FET 1e-4 hold tail >100 aA at -3.0 V, ring tail >100 aA, or disturb >1 LSB; the closure coupon is then never released. Kill the single-etch leg if there is no write-then-read closure by M18. Only the coaxial fallback (~1.5-2.5x bits/$) would then remain, and that is not a moonshot raise.

sequence: Pre-M0 (Nov-Dec 2026), ~$0: recruit the oxide-reliability co-founder. Read imec IEDM 2024 37-6 (Kishore et al.) and IMW 2026 to learn CHARGE-RIVER's CTE definition, and drop its CCD split if the 98% is per transfer and buried/fat-zero gives <2x. Read US 12,666,958 and US 2025/0167193 (HOT-SIDE) and the NEO and Macronix claims (AND-STACK). Sign Purdue Birck and GT IEN user agreements. Order retired DDR4, DDR5 RDIMMs and Bender FPGAs.

1. Campaign C1, DRAM ERROR ATLAS (M0-M6, $110k): RAW-BER Phase 1 on DRAM Bender and Antmicro. It is the fastest binary, and its VRT, cluster and dwell-time statistics become the shared error model for every cell's 1e-4 budget.

2. Campaign C2, OXIDE TAIL ATLAS (M1-M11, $280k + $70k side splits): ONE shared planar IGZO/IGO/ZTO lot at Purdue Birck (GT IEN second source) on a sky130 carrier with an on-coupon 15 ns dual sample-and-hold. One wafer set serves six concepts: >=1e5-cell vertical 2T0C arrays, with a D2O real-bond split, for HOT-SIDE Gate A+; 65k oxide source followers for the ns-RTN 1e-4 quantile (PIXEL-STACK residual, MARGIN STACK gain FET, DIODE-TOWER gain FET, CHARGE-RIVER FD-SF); >=1e6 hybrid 2T leakage cells for the aged 2e-5 quantile (MARGIN STACK K2) and the write-FET tail at -3.0 V hold (AND-STACK GO#1A); 1x/2x/4x cumulative H-dose splits (PIXEL-STACK retention). Side splits: AND-STACK planar CR/disturb ($35k), DIODE-TOWER integrable-anode Schottky RuO2/MoOx/WOx ($20k), and a minimal surface-vs-buried CCD ($15k, only if the imec read passes).
3. Campaign C3, AND-STACK 2-tier vertical closure coupon (M9-M14, $120k): released only at the M9 atlas gate. It is the moonshot option.

4. Campaign C4, HOT-SIDE Gate B-lite (M11-M18, $70k): released only at Gate A+. Oxide tiers go on finished sky130 (or partner GF/Intel) logic die, with RO/Vt shift, 1,000 h bake, CSAM on bonded pairs and VPD-ICPMS. In parallel, open BSPDN partner talks (Intel Foundry 18A/14A first, as the U.S. backside-power host).

5. M18-M24: commit the reserve to the winner and build a measured-not-modeled data room. Raise $10-50M on HOT-SIDE, with AND-STACK as the upside option if GO#1B closed. Deferred to the raise or to partners: the MARGIN STACK 22FDX MPW (its decisive oxide terms come from C2 for free), the PIXEL-STACK 4-tier stack, CELL-WAFER bond daisy chains, the full CHARGE-RIVER matrix and the AND-STACK 32-tier etch coupon.

Not funded with venture dollars: LEAN ARRAY MODULE goes to a grant or OEM JDA track (Sandia CRADA, NSF SBIR; ~3% of DRAM helium, nothing to own). AI MEMORY DIET (1.17x wafer-eq, S=1) and CELL-WAFER FOUNDRY (inherits the cell's risk; the split adds only ~1.5x capex) are not funded either.
gates: M0: the imec CTE definition is read, so the CCD split is kept or dropped. The FTO claim reads are done, and the device co-founder has signed.

M3 G0: Bender stations and the aA/ns bench reproduce published DDR4 retention and IGZO 2T0C retention within 2x. Atlas mask frozen with all six concepts' structures. HOT-SIDE trace study: >=50% of bytes from <=30% of resident bytes, else carry the capacity-indexed ~90 W.

M6 G1 (RAW-BER): GO if the chipkill safe interval incl. VRT is >=6x the JEDEC window at 85 C, multi-chip events are <=10%, and the 1 h grade holds for >=95% of modules. Then publish the error atlas, seek a hyperscaler soak partner, and keep the 1e-4 contract in every cell budget. KILL if <4x at 65 C, and re-plan all cells without the 1.88x margin.

M8-M9 G2 (ATLAS planar read): write-FET 1e-4 hold tail, ns-RTN 1e-4 quantile, fresh 2e-5 leakage quantile, AND planar CR. Release C3 ($120k) only if the tail is <=100 aA at -3 V and CR >=0.40 (targets <=17 aA, >=0.57). Kill DIODE-TOWER if every integrable anode exceeds 928 aA ring leakage at 85 C. Kill the CCD split if buried deferral is <3x surface. Flag PIXEL-STACK go/no-go on SF RTN (<=40 mV plan residual).

M11 G3 (HOT-SIDE Gate A+, incl. real D2O bond): a 1 b PASS (drift <=75 mV, RTN <=100 mV, tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C, bonded dVt <=10 mV) releases C4, files the bond-H and cross-T MLC provisionals and opens BSPDN talks. If every split fails, the capacity claim is dead and the lead thesis passes to AND-STACK or PIXEL-STACK on atlas data. Also read MARGIN STACK K2: the aged 2e-5 quantile after 1,000 h at 105 C must be <=586 aA.
M14 G4 (AND-STACK GO#1B): 2-tier write-then-read, no short, ring hold <=100 aA, CR >=0.57, FIB/TEM. PASS starts JDA outreach to Kioxia/SanDisk, Macronix and Micron. Hard stop at M18 if not closed.
M18 G5 (HOT-SIDE Gate B-lite): RO shift <=1%, Vt <=10 mV under 2 tiers after a 1,000 h bake, void-free CSAM, In/Ga/Zn <=1e10 at/cm2.

M18-M20 G6 (raise gate): one measured headline. Either HOT-SIDE A+ and B pass plus a named BSPDN evaluator letter, or AND-STACK closure plus a NAND-maker MTA. Neither means no raise: sell or license the atlas data and IP and return capital.

honest_framing: Physics was rarely the wall: 12,857 ideas narrowed to ten concepts and 181 objections, and nothing died on physics. All ten were downgraded, typically by ~2x on the headline (AND-STACK 8.1x -> 5.9x density and 3.8x -> 2.3x bits/$; HOT-SIDE ~190 -> ~90 W/GPU; RAW-BER 15x -> 9x; MARGIN STACK EV 75 -> 24; CHARGE-RIVER's cost leg killed). The real openings are where incumbents' constraints differ from physics: aA-leakage oxide semiconductors make refresh-light memory at junction temperature possible, so a ~10x survives on energy per bit moved, not on cost. NAND-style single-etch tiering is the one route to a multi-x density step, but it rests on process modules nobody has built. Against incumbents moving 8-12%/yr and already building 4F2/VCT and 3D DRAM, $/bit steps shrink to ~1.1-1.6x by 2032, and broad architecture claims sit inside SEL, Macronix, imec and NEO prior art. A startup's defensible value is therefore narrow, measured know-how: tail statistics, hydrogen control and read tricks. Persistence can grind down engineering terms (RTN screening, ECC budgets, H barriers, new modules), and each got a priced redesign. It cannot beat a topological impossibility (the single-film AND closure), a bandwidth wall (the 26.7x all-layer latent), the absence of an integrable >=1.0 eV oxide Schottky if nature does not supply one, or the fact that 64-tier yield and foundry slots are only provable with partners' money.
biggest_unknown: The statistical tails of scaled amorphous-oxide transistors (IGZO/IGO/ZTO, <=0.01-0.02 um2) after the full <=400 C hydrogen, thermal and bonding budget at 85-125 C. Two numbers matter: the 1e-4 to 2e-5 quantile of aA-level off-state leakage, and the 1e-4 quantile of ns-timescale RTN. Published data describe median cells (e.g. '>200 s at 95 C'). The red team moved every cell concept on this one unmeasured term, and HOT-SIDE's tail multiplier went from 3x to 25x (91x unmitigated). The thresholds that decide each concept: HOT-SIDE tail <=22.5 aA at 125 C and RTN <=100/30 mV; AND-STACK write-FET tail <=17 aA at -3 V hold; MARGIN STACK aged 2e-5 quantile <=586 aA and RTN <=44 mV; PIXEL-STACK SF residual <=40 mV and tail <=45-90 aA; DIODE-TOWER RTN <=25 mV; CHARGE-RIVER FD-SF 1e-9 step <=30 e-. Whether the tail is ~3x or ~90x the median picks the winner, so one shared atlas lot is worth more than any single-concept experiment.
monday_action: Three steps, 2 hours total. (1) 45 min: merge the six concepts' tail thresholds (listed under biggest_unknown) from dossier sections 5 and 11 into a one-page 'Oxide Tail Atlas' test-structure spec covering device count, area, timescale, temperature, H-dose and bond splits, and the pass line per concept. (2) 45 min: send that page to Purdue Birck (Peide Ye's group) and Georgia Tech IEN (Datta/Khan groups), asking for two things: a user-facility quote and slot for one shared planar lot starting Jan 2027, and whether they already hold >=1e4-device leakage or RTN CDFs to the 1e-4 quantile that could settle a threshold before any spend. (3) 30 min: buy and read imec IEDM 2024 paper 37-6 (DOI 10.1109/iedm50854.2024.10873539) to learn whether 'CTE >98%' is per transfer or end-to-end. That decides whether CHARGE-RIVER's CCD split goes on the atlas mask at all.
recruit_first: First recruit (the co-founder): an oxide-semiconductor device-reliability physicist. That means IGZO/IGO/ZTO PBTI, hydrogen and RTN, plus aA floating-node leakage-tail metrology on >=1e4-device arrays, ideally with 2T0C gain-cell experience. This person owns the shared tail atlas, HOT-SIDE Gate A+ and AND-STACK GO#1A. Recruit from imec's IGZO 2T0C DRAM team (G. S. Kar's group and alumni), Purdue (Peide Ye's group), Georgia Tech (Suman Datta, Asif Khan and Shimeng Yu groups), Stanford (H.-S. Philip Wong, Krishna Saraswat), Intel Components Research (BEOL oxide transistors), or the Kioxia/Nanya OCTRAM, Micron and Samsung/SK hynix oxide-DRAM programs. Affiliations are as listed in the dossiers, from training knowledge, and unverified. Next, as contractors or advisors: a CMOS image-sensor CDS/readout designer (OmniVision, onsemi, Sony, Gigajot) for the 15 ns sample-and-hold and RTN statistics, and a DRAM Bender-experienced test engineer (ETH SAFARI or CMU lineage) for C1.
facility_first: Purdue Birck Nanotechnology Center (West Lafayette, IN). It offers IGZO/IGO/ZTO ALD and vertical channel-all-around 2T0C coupons (Ye group), and the dossiers name it for HOT-SIDE Gate A+ and the PIXEL-STACK planar lot, so it hosts the shared Oxide Tail Atlas. Georgia Tech IEN is the parallel second source. SkyWater sky130 (Minnesota) shuttles supply the U.S.-made readout and logic-proxy die. MIT Lincoln Laboratory or NY CREATES (Albany) follow for bonding, BSPDN-carrier emulation and the 32-tier etch coupon at the raise.
correction_2026_11_04: Correction added 2026-11-04 by the study owner, not by the judge: the '~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL' figure quoted above gave DDR4 the 128 check bits of a DDR5 RDIMM line; a DDR4 x4 ECC RDIMM carries 64 per 64 B line. The corrected model (models/raw-ber-contract.py section 10.11) gives ~11x with two channels in lockstep (6.9x pessimistic, 7x with a chip dead) and ~4x on one channel (3.4x pessimistic, none with a chip dead); ~13x needs 11.1% of DDR4 capacity spent on extra check bits. The text above is left as written; the DDR5 figures are unaffected. See dossiers/raw-ber-contract.md section 12.1.
